21.01.01.context: An API logs an order lookup that includes a private request body.
21.01.01.concept: Structured records should use stable fields and explicit allowlists; redaction is a second defense, not permission to log secrets.
21.01.01.exercise: Run safeLog with a synthetic password field; configure a real Pino logger to emit selected fields only and inspect its output.
21.01.01.positive: Output has request ID, route template, status and duration; no password.
21.01.01.negative: A raw body or authorization value in logs fails review.
21.01.01.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.01.02.context: Two services handle the same request through a proxy.
21.01.02.concept: Correlation IDs connect records, but untrusted header values need validation; trace context is not authentication.
21.01.02.exercise: Propagate a bounded generated ID through two local handlers, and submit malformed and overlong IDs.
21.01.02.positive: Both handlers log the same valid correlation ID.
21.01.02.negative: Invalid input is rejected or replaced; no permission is granted by an ID.
21.01.02.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.01.03.context: An operator needs counts, queue depth and latency distributions.
21.01.03.concept: Counters accumulate events, gauges report current state, histograms group observations into buckets; units and labels must be stable.
21.01.03.exercise: Design request_total, queue_depth and request_duration_seconds metrics; record three requests and a queue drain.
21.01.03.positive: Counter grows, gauge falls, histogram observes three durations.
21.01.03.negative: A request ID as metric label or a decrementing request counter fails.
21.01.03.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.01.04.context: A checkout calls inventory then payment.
21.01.04.concept: A trace links causally related spans with parent relationships, durations and statuses; context propagation crosses process boundaries.
21.01.04.exercise: Sketch a root checkout span and two child spans. In an installed tracing fixture cause payment failure and inspect parent IDs.
21.01.04.positive: Both children belong to the checkout trace and payment reports failure.
21.01.04.negative: Orphan spans or a swallowed dependency error obscure the cause.
21.01.04.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.01.05.context: An HTTP server needs repeatable tracing before application startup.
21.01.05.concept: Instrument supported libraries before loading them, configure resource identity and export via a controlled collector.
21.01.05.exercise: Build a disposable Node service with the OpenTelemetry SDK, start instrumentation first, send one loopback request and inspect the exported trace.
21.01.05.positive: Exporter contains a service name and request span.
21.01.05.negative: Missing instrumentation or exporter failure is not a passing trace test.
21.01.05.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.01.06.context: An exception report contains a synthetic access token.
21.01.06.concept: Error tracking groups crashes and captures context; scrub secrets before sending, and restrict access/retention.
21.01.06.exercise: In an isolated Sentry test transport, trigger an exception with fake sensitive context and inspect the event before transmission.
21.01.06.positive: Exception is actionable without secret context.
21.01.06.negative: Fake token appearing in a report fails the privacy gate.
21.01.06.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.01.07.context: A metric uses user IDs as labels.
21.01.07.concept: High cardinality increases series count; sampling controls trace volume but can bias observed data.
21.01.07.exercise: Compare unique label counts for 100 users versus 3 route templates; specify a sampling policy and document errors that might be missed.
21.01.07.positive: Bounded templates yield a small number of series.
21.01.07.negative: Per-user labels explode series count; sampled data cannot prove every request traced.
21.01.07.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.01.08.context: A learner investigates a failing API call.
21.01.08.concept: Combine correlation ID, span timing, logs and aggregate metrics without exposing payloads.
21.01.08.exercise: Run safeLog tests; in a local instrumented API provoke a synthetic downstream error, connect its span and log, record the evidence.
21.01.08.positive: One trace identifies the failing dependency and matching safe log.
21.01.08.negative: Missing parent context, leaking credentials, or unobserved error fails.
21.01.08.boundary: Local field-allowlist model only; Pino, exporters, collectors and Sentry require installed tools and actual trace propagation.

21.02.01.context: An API has a 99% successful-request objective.
21.02.01.concept: SLI measures a defined population, SLO sets its target, and error budget is the permitted failure fraction over a window.
21.02.01.exercise: Run errorBudget(1000,10,.99) and then 11 failures; define which requests count.
21.02.01.positive: Ten failures exhaust but do not exceed the budget.
21.02.01.negative: Eleven failures breach; zero traffic does not establish reliability.
21.02.01.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.02.02.context: An on-call engineer receives one page per transient failure.
21.02.02.concept: Page on actionable user-impact symptoms and sustained burn; deduplicate alerts and assign an owner.
21.02.02.exercise: Draw a timeline with one transient error and sustained failures; define fast and slow burn thresholds plus escalation.
21.02.02.positive: Sustained budget burn produces one actionable page.
21.02.02.negative: A noisy non-actionable page or silence during sustained impact fails.
21.02.02.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.02.03.context: An app is alive but cannot serve traffic.
21.02.03.concept: Liveness indicates whether restart may help; readiness indicates traffic eligibility. Avoid using dependent DB outages as unconditional restart triggers.
21.02.03.exercise: Design separate loopback endpoints; stop a disposable dependency and query both.
21.02.03.positive: Readiness fails while process liveness remains healthy.
21.02.03.negative: Routing to an unready service or restart loops fail.
21.02.03.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.02.04.context: A remote dependency repeatedly times out.
21.02.04.concept: A circuit breaker opens after a failure rule, rejects calls during cooldown and probes recovery in half-open state.
21.02.04.exercise: Design a fake-clock breaker with three failures and one half-open probe; record transitions.
21.02.04.positive: Open state short-circuits calls; successful probe closes.
21.02.04.negative: Unbounded probes or immediate retry storms fail.
21.02.04.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.02.05.context: A checkout retries a slow payment request.
21.02.05.concept: Use a total deadline, bounded attempts, jitter and idempotency; retry transient failures only.
21.02.05.exercise: Evaluate retryDecision from 23.04 for transient and permanent errors, with deadline exhausted.
21.02.05.positive: A safe transient retry fits remaining deadline.
21.02.05.negative: Non-idempotent or expired request must stop.
21.02.05.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.02.06.context: One slow endpoint occupies every worker.
21.02.06.concept: Bulkheads isolate resource pools; backpressure bounds work rather than allowing unbounded queues.
21.02.06.exercise: Construct a disposable pool with two workers and a maximum queue of three; fill it with synthetic tasks.
21.02.06.positive: Other isolated work still runs; saturation rejects or delays explicitly.
21.02.06.negative: Unbounded queue growth and starvation fail.
21.02.06.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.02.07.concept: Graceful degradation preserves the critical user journey while labeling unavailable optional data; avoid serving unauthorized cached data.
21.02.07.exercise: Design checkout with optional recommendations, simulate timeout and show an explicit fallback.
21.02.07.positive: Checkout remains available with a fallback.
21.02.07.negative: A stale private response or misleading success fails.
21.02.07.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.02.08.context: A team rehearses a dependency failure.
21.02.08.concept: Fault injection begins with a hypothesis, bounded blast radius, abort condition and recovery measurement.
21.02.08.exercise: Inject deterministic failures into an isolated handler; calculate budget, remove fault, and compare recovery samples.
21.02.08.positive: Measured failure and recovery match the defined target.
21.02.08.negative: Unbounded fault injection or missing recovery evidence fails.
21.02.08.boundary: Synthetic error-budget arithmetic only; real probes, alerts, concurrency and fault recovery require actual isolated services.

21.03.01.context: Checkout is unavailable and no owner has been assigned.
21.03.01.concept: Severity follows user impact; name an incident commander, technical lead and communications owner.
21.03.01.exercise: Run incidentDecision with unavailable and no owner; draft role assignment for the exercise.
21.03.01.positive: High impact receives SEV1 and escalation in this local rubric.
21.03.01.negative: Unowned high-impact incident cannot be marked handled.
21.03.01.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

21.03.02.context: An alert says latency is high without a next action.
21.03.02.concept: A runbook links symptoms to dashboards, safe diagnostics, mitigation, escalation and rollback; record last validation.
21.03.02.exercise: Write a one-page runbook for rising p95 and rehearse with synthetic samples.
21.03.02.positive: Operator can identify queue versus work time and mitigation.
21.03.02.negative: A destructive step without guardrails or missing owner fails.
21.03.02.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

21.03.03.context: Logs persist user data longer than necessary.
21.03.03.concept: Retention follows legitimate purpose, access control and deletion policy; avoid logging unnecessary personal data.
21.03.03.exercise: Create synthetic log files with two retention classes, define expiry and verify a dry-run deletion list.
21.03.03.positive: Only expired eligible records are selected.
21.03.03.negative: Private payloads or unbounded retention fail policy.
21.03.03.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

21.03.04.context: A database backup job reports success every night.
21.03.04.concept: A backup is not recoverability evidence until restored and validated with integrity and application checks.
21.03.04.exercise: On a disposable DB restore synthetic backup into a different database, check counts and application behavior.
21.03.04.positive: Restore works and measured duration is recorded.
21.03.04.negative: Corrupted backup or missing restore test is not recovery proof.
21.03.04.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

21.03.05.context: A service can tolerate limited data loss and downtime.
21.03.05.concept: RPO bounds recoverable data loss; RTO bounds restoration time. Set them from business needs and test against real drills.
21.03.05.exercise: Model last recoverable snapshot and restore duration; compare against chosen RPO/RTO.
21.03.05.negative: A recent backup with restore exceeding RTO still fails.
21.03.05.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

21.03.06.context: An outage recurs after a blame-focused report.
21.03.06.concept: A blameless postmortem records timeline, impact, contributing causes, mitigations and owned corrective actions.
21.03.06.exercise: Write a synthetic incident timeline and one action with owner, due date and verification criterion.
21.03.06.positive: Actions address system conditions and can be tested.
21.03.06.negative: Blaming an individual without corrective evidence fails.
21.03.06.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

21.03.07.context: Traffic rises before a planned sales campaign.
21.03.07.concept: Capacity planning combines measured throughput, saturation, headroom, cost and demand uncertainty.
21.03.07.exercise: Use capacity from 22.03 for a demand range and record assumptions about a database limit.
21.03.07.negative: Forecasting only CPU while DB connections saturate fails.
21.03.07.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

21.03.08.context: An API outage requires coordination and recovery.
21.03.08.concept: Incident drills exercise detection, assignment, mitigation, communications and validation without touching live services.
21.03.08.exercise: Run incidentDecision; simulate unavailable dependency, assign roles, restore disposable fixture, record timestamps.
21.03.08.positive: Recovery evidence and owner are recorded independently.
21.03.08.negative: Declaring recovery without functional verification fails.
21.03.08.boundary: Synthetic incident decisions only; no real emergency response, restored backups, alerting or production capacity measurements.

22.01.01.context: A page loads slowly, responds late and shifts layout.
22.01.01.concept: LCP measures largest content render timing, INP interaction responsiveness, CLS unexpected layout movement; assess field distributions separately from lab runs.
22.01.01.exercise: Use webBudget with example 2500ms LCP, 200ms INP, .1 CLS; then collect a real browser trace and record its conditions.
22.01.01.positive: Independent budgets are evaluated, not averaged.
22.01.01.negative: Missing INP or unstable layout cannot pass by fast LCP alone.
22.01.01.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.01.02.context: A small page ships an oversized client bundle.
22.01.02.concept: Inspect dependency composition, transfer size and parse/execute cost; split or remove work based on evidence.
22.01.02.exercise: In a built disposable Next app inspect bundle output before and after removing an unused heavy dependency.
22.01.02.positive: Relevant client chunk shrinks with unchanged behavior.
22.01.02.negative: Only changing source file size without measuring output is insufficient.
22.01.02.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.01.03.context: A server-rendered page waits on a slow secondary panel.
22.01.03.concept: Streaming can deliver ready content early with Suspense boundaries; hydration and errors still require testing.
22.01.03.exercise: Build an isolated route with delayed secondary data and record first bytes, visible content and final panel.
22.01.03.positive: Primary UI appears before slow panel; loading state is accessible.
22.01.03.negative: Blank shell or leaked unauthorized content fails.
22.01.03.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.01.04.context: A hero image and web font delay meaningful content.
22.01.04.concept: Choose responsive image sizes, reserved dimensions, suitable formats and limited critical font loading.
22.01.04.exercise: Measure a disposable page before/after responsive assets and explicit dimensions under fixed browser settings.
22.01.04.positive: Lower transfer and stable layout with acceptable visual quality.
22.01.04.negative: Preloading every asset or dimensionless image regressions fail.
22.01.04.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.01.05.context: A page eagerly prefetches every link.
22.01.05.concept: Hints consume bandwidth and connections; prioritize only probable navigations and critical assets.
22.01.05.exercise: Record network requests with and without targeted prefetch under throttling; compare navigation and current page metrics.
22.01.05.positive: Useful prefetch improves next navigation without starving critical resources.
22.01.05.negative: Extra traffic worsening first-page budget fails.
22.01.05.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.01.06.context: A page waits for sequential dependent requests.
22.01.06.concept: Waterfall analysis identifies dependency chains, connection delays and render-blocking resources.
22.01.06.exercise: In DevTools inspect a local page with sequential requests; parallelize independent requests and compare traces.
22.01.06.positive: Critical path shortens while dependent data ordering stays valid.
22.01.06.negative: Parallelizing dependent or unauthorized requests fails.
22.01.06.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.01.07.context: A list renders ten thousand rows at once.
22.01.07.concept: Virtualization bounds DOM work by visible range and overscan; preserve semantics, focus and scroll position.
22.01.07.exercise: Render a synthetic long list with and without virtualization; measure DOM nodes and keyboard behavior.
22.01.07.positive: DOM count remains bounded; focus remains usable.
22.01.07.negative: Missing reachable rows or lost keyboard focus fails.
22.01.07.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.01.08.context: A team needs a repeatable frontend performance gate.
22.01.08.concept: Set explicit metric and transfer budgets with controlled conditions; distinguish lab and field evidence.
22.01.08.exercise: Run webBudget, add a one-byte regression and one missing metric; then plan browser runs on fixed fixtures.
22.01.08.positive: All required metrics within budget passes the model.
22.01.08.negative: Missing or exceeded metrics fail; synthetic values are not browser proof.
22.01.08.boundary: Synthetic measured-value budget only; actual Core Web Vitals, browser profiles and real-user metrics are unexecuted.

22.02.01.context: A Node server becomes CPU-bound under workload.
22.02.01.concept: CPU profiling identifies hot stacks; heap snapshots describe retained objects and may contain secrets or pause the process.
22.02.01.exercise: Profile a disposable CPU-heavy loop and compare before/after change under fixed workload; inspect sanitized heap data separately.
22.02.01.positive: Hot function is measurable and improvement is repeatable.
22.02.01.negative: A single unrepresentative timing or real private heap dump fails review.
22.02.01.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.02.02.context: A team assumes switching frameworks fixes p95.
22.02.02.concept: Compare identical workload, validation, payload, concurrency, runtime and hardware; framework benchmarks do not establish app gains.
22.02.02.exercise: Run isolated equivalent Fastify and alternative endpoints with warmup and repeated trials; compare error rate and latency.
22.02.02.positive: Comparison has matched conditions and documented variance.
22.02.02.negative: Different business logic or omitted errors invalidates result.
22.02.02.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.02.03.concept: Pool sizing depends on DB capacity, service instances, query time and queue limits, not only app CPU.
22.02.03.exercise: Use requestProfile on synthetic queue/work samples; in a disposable DB compare two bounded pool settings.
22.02.03.positive: Queue and execution measurements are separate.
22.02.03.negative: Larger pool causing DB saturation or errors is not an improvement.
22.02.03.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.02.04.context: An endpoint queries child rows once per parent.
22.02.04.concept: N+1 increases round trips; inspect plans and query count before choosing joins, batching or indexes.
22.02.04.exercise: Seed a disposable DB with 20 parents; count queries and inspect EXPLAIN, then compare a bounded batch.
22.02.04.positive: Query count decreases while result and authorization remain correct.
22.02.04.negative: An unbounded join or missing tenant filter fails.
22.02.04.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.02.05.context: Clients repeatedly fetch an unchanged resource.
22.02.05.concept: ETag validators allow conditional requests; cache identity includes representation and auth policy.
22.02.05.exercise: Use a local HTTP fixture with an ETag; send If-None-Match and then mutate resource.
22.02.05.positive: Unchanged response returns 304 and changed representation returns 200.
22.02.05.negative: A private response cached across users or stale validator fails.
22.02.05.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.02.06.context: A large JSON response consumes bandwidth.
22.02.06.concept: Compression trades CPU for transfer size; respect content negotiation and avoid unsafe secret-bearing compression patterns.
22.02.06.exercise: Benchmark local synthetic public JSON with and without compression; record size, CPU and p95.
22.02.06.positive: Transfer size improves within CPU/error budget.
22.02.06.negative: Unacceptable CPU increase or incorrect Content-Encoding fails.
22.02.06.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.02.07.context: An API combines many small reads.
22.02.07.concept: Batching reduces overhead but increases wait time and per-batch failure scope; bound size and preserve per-item auth.
22.02.07.exercise: Design a batch of ten authorized requests plus one foreign tenant item; compare latency and outcomes.
22.02.07.positive: Authorized items return correctly; unauthorized item denied.
22.02.07.negative: A batch that bypasses individual authorization fails.
22.02.07.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.02.08.context: A service must reduce p95 without hiding errors.
22.02.08.concept: Measure queue time, execution and total per request; percentiles are not additive across distributions.
22.02.08.exercise: Run requestProfile on matched synthetic pairs; then benchmark a real disposable API before and after one change.
22.02.08.positive: Total p95 computed from per-request sums; errors reported separately.
22.02.08.negative: Adding queue p95 and work p95 or dropping failures is invalid.
22.02.08.boundary: Synthetic latency sample analysis only; actual CPU/heap profiles, Fastify comparison, query plans and HTTP behavior need real runtimes.

22.03.01.context: An edge cache serves an outdated product page.
22.03.01.concept: CDN cache keys, TTL, invalidation and versioned assets define freshness; private content needs explicit isolation.
22.03.01.exercise: Design public catalog and authenticated cart cache policies; in a local proxy test update and invalidation.
22.03.01.positive: Catalog converges and cart remains private.
22.03.01.negative: Cross-user cache leakage or stale version after purge fails.
22.03.01.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

22.03.02.context: An app has browser, CDN, process and Redis caches.
22.03.02.concept: Each cache tier has distinct ownership, scope, TTL and failure mode; name authoritative state.
22.03.02.exercise: Map keys and TTL per tier; simulate origin update and process-cache miss.
22.03.02.positive: Authoritative read remains correct despite tier misses.
22.03.02.negative: A private value in shared public cache fails.
22.03.02.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

22.03.03.context: An order update races with cache invalidation.
22.03.03.concept: Cache-aside can expose stale data; version checks and invalidation after commit reduce races, not eliminate every stale read.
22.03.03.exercise: Design versioned cached row with versions 2 and 3; simulate delayed invalidation and stale refill.
22.03.03.negative: Late stale write restoring outdated state fails.
22.03.03.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

22.03.04.context: An API has two load-balanced instances.
22.03.04.concept: Stateless application requests can be served by any healthy instance; session/state must be external or explicitly routed.
22.03.04.exercise: Rehearse a local two-instance fixture with one stopped instance and repeated requests.
22.03.04.positive: Healthy remaining instance serves authorized requests.
22.03.04.negative: In-process session loss or routing to unhealthy instance fails.
22.03.04.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

22.03.05.context: Demand doubles under an instance limit.
22.03.05.concept: Horizontal scaling needs measured per-instance capacity and headroom, with downstream constraints.
22.03.05.exercise: Use capacity for 160 rps, 100 per instance, 20% headroom and cap two; change demand to 161.
22.03.05.positive: Two instances meet first scenario; next needs three.
22.03.05.negative: Demand above cap cannot be reported feasible.
22.03.05.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

22.03.06.context: A small team must scale under a strict budget.
22.03.06.concept: Use measured workload and marginal cost, caps and service limits; avoid autoscaling without spend controls.
22.03.06.exercise: Compare two synthetic scenarios by required instances and assumed per-instance cost; record assumptions.
22.03.06.positive: Plan meets budget and explicitly names unresolved bottlenecks.
22.03.06.negative: Ignoring fixed DB or egress cost invalidates comparison.
22.03.06.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

22.03.07.context: A performance improvement may regress next release.
22.03.07.concept: Baseline captures version, workload, conditions and distributions; repeat trials and use defined thresholds.
22.03.07.exercise: Store synthetic baseline and changed result, then plan matched real benchmark runs.
22.03.07.positive: Regression gate catches meaningful increase under equivalent conditions.
22.03.07.negative: Comparing different hardware/workload or ignoring variance fails.
22.03.07.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

22.03.08.context: A learner forecasts peak capacity for a small SaaS.
22.03.08.concept: A forecast is a scenario with uncertainty, not a guarantee; combine throughput, headroom and hard dependency limits.
22.03.08.exercise: Run capacity for low, expected and high demand; document DB connection and budget constraints.
22.03.08.positive: Forecast gives required instances and feasibility for each scenario.
22.03.08.negative: Impossible resource cap or missing measurement cannot qualify capacity.
22.03.08.boundary: Capacity arithmetic only; no actual CDN, cache cluster, balancing, cost quotes or scaling benchmark.

23.01.01.context: A service class handles orders, email, billing and formatting.
23.01.01.concept: High cohesion groups related decisions; coupling measures dependency and change impact. SOLID guides design, not class count.
23.01.01.exercise: Draw responsibilities and dependency edges; separate order rules from email delivery using a port.
23.01.01.positive: Order policy can change without modifying the sender.
23.01.01.negative: New cyclic dependencies or abstractions without a reason fail.
23.01.01.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.01.02.context: Domain logic imports a concrete ORM client.
23.01.02.concept: Dependency inversion makes higher-level policy depend on an abstraction it owns; infrastructure implements it.
23.01.02.exercise: Use boundaryViolations to forbid domain-to-ORM and allow usecase-to-port; implement a fake port.
23.01.02.positive: Policy tests run without ORM connection.
23.01.02.negative: Concrete ORM dependency in domain fails.
23.01.02.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.01.03.context: A use case must support HTTP and CLI entry points.
23.01.03.concept: Ports define required/provided capabilities; adapters translate outside protocols into use-case inputs.
23.01.03.exercise: Design submit-order port and two adapters; exercise same invariant through both.
23.01.03.positive: Both adapters use the same application contract.
23.01.03.negative: Duplicated business rule or adapter bypass fails.
23.01.03.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.01.04.context: A business service calls an external payment API.
23.01.04.concept: Hexagonal architecture separates core behavior from outside input/output technology.
23.01.04.exercise: Draw inbound order adapter, domain/usecase and outbound payment port; test fake payment response.
23.01.04.positive: Core changes independently of the adapter.
23.01.04.negative: Framework types or HTTP errors leaking into domain fail.
23.01.04.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.01.05.context: A simple CRUD app grows multiple layers of mapping.
23.01.05.concept: Clean architecture prioritizes dependency direction and replaceable boundaries; extra layers have maintenance cost.
23.01.05.exercise: Compare direct CRUD module versus domain-rich module and justify each boundary using change scenarios.
23.01.05.positive: Chosen design solves actual coupling and test needs.
23.01.05.negative: Adding abstractions with no change or testing benefit is unjustified.
23.01.05.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.01.06.context: A domain money value is stored in database columns.
23.01.06.concept: Domain models represent invariants; persistence models represent storage and mapping. They may coincide for simple CRUD.
23.01.06.exercise: Define a money invariant and map synthetic storage rows to domain values; reject invalid row.
23.01.06.positive: Valid storage yields a valid domain value.
23.01.06.negative: Negative or malformed amount cannot bypass invariant.
23.01.06.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.01.07.context: A team must choose monolith or service extraction.
23.01.07.concept: An ADR records context, decision, alternatives, consequences and reconsideration triggers.
23.01.07.exercise: Write a short ADR for keeping a module in-process, with measured trigger for extraction.
23.01.07.negative: An ADR with only a preferred tool and no consequences fails.
23.01.07.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.01.08.concept: Architecture diagrams should show directed dependencies, ownership and trust boundaries rather than only boxes.
23.01.08.exercise: Define allowed edges and use boundaryViolations to test one forbidden domain-to-infrastructure dependency.
23.01.08.negative: Reversed or forbidden dependency is flagged.
23.01.08.boundary: Directed dependency model only; no actual codebase static graph, framework migration or architecture certification.

23.02.01.context: Orders and inventory share one application but different data rules.
23.02.01.concept: Domain modules own behavior and persistence boundaries; a monolith can have independent internal contracts.
23.02.01.exercise: Draw order/inventory ownership and explicit allowed dependencies; remove direct cross-module writes.
23.02.01.positive: Each module controls its own data mutations.
23.02.01.negative: A module editing another module's private table without contract fails.
23.02.01.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.02.02.context: Billing calls order module internals directly.
23.02.02.concept: Public module interfaces define stable behavior; internals remain private and versioned as needed.
23.02.02.exercise: Design getOrderSummary interface returning minimal DTO; replace internal representation and test contract.
23.02.02.positive: Consumer behavior stays stable after internal refactor.
23.02.02.negative: Importing private entity or exposing secrets fails.
23.02.02.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.02.03.context: Order placement needs inventory and payment invariants.
23.02.03.concept: A local transaction can enforce same-database invariants; outside side effects need separate coordination and compensation.
23.02.03.exercise: In disposable DB reserve stock and create order in one transaction; force failure and roll back.
23.02.03.positive: Both writes commit or neither does.
23.02.03.negative: Partial committed state or external call inside blind retry fails.
23.02.03.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.02.04.concept: Domain events describe meaningful past facts; publication should follow committed changes, with durability when needed.
23.02.04.exercise: Define OrderPlaced event and local handler; distinguish precommit in-process signal from durable outbox event.
23.02.04.positive: Committed order produces expected event contract.
23.02.04.negative: Rollback publishing a misleading committed event fails.
23.02.04.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.02.05.context: Use-case tests need to replace a database repository.
23.02.05.concept: Repositories express domain persistence needs rather than exposing arbitrary query builders.
23.02.05.exercise: Define reserve and lookup port; test in-memory fake and separately test DB adapter contract.
23.02.05.positive: Fake exercises use case; real adapter meets same behavior.
23.02.05.negative: Repository exposing unrestricted foreign-tenant reads fails.
23.02.05.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.02.06.context: A module feature needs gradual enablement.
23.02.06.concept: Feature toggles have default, scope, ownership and expiry; flags are not authorization.
23.02.06.exercise: Design stable subject assignment with default-off; check authorized and unauthorized users.
23.02.06.positive: Flag changes exposure for authorized cohort only.
23.02.06.negative: Flag overriding permission or missing default fails.
23.02.06.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.02.07.context: Three modules want a shared utility library.
23.02.07.concept: Shared kernel should be small and stable; domain-specific rules belong to their owner.
23.02.07.exercise: Classify date parsing versus order discount rule; draw dependencies before moving code.
23.02.07.positive: Shared utility has no dependency on domain modules.
23.02.07.negative: Shared kernel becoming a dependency hub for business rules fails.
23.02.07.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.02.08.context: Orders imports billing, billing imports inventory, inventory imports orders.
23.02.08.concept: Dependency cycles make initialization and ownership unclear; introduce a contract or orchestrator with a directed graph.
23.02.08.exercise: Run dependencyCycle with indirect cycle then extract one shared port or coordinating use case.
23.02.08.negative: Self or indirect cycle remains detectable.
23.02.08.boundary: Small synthetic dependency graph only; real module enforcement, transactions and feature flag runtime not executed.

23.03.01.context: An order service receives a request and announces the result.
23.03.01.concept: Commands express intent and may be rejected; events record facts and are named in past tense.
23.03.01.exercise: Design ReserveStock command and StockReserved event; handle invalid quantity before emitting event.
23.03.01.negative: Rejected command cannot emit a success event.
23.03.01.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.03.02.context: A read model updates asynchronously after an order commits.
23.03.02.concept: Eventual consistency permits temporary staleness; communicate lag and provide safe authoritative paths where needed.
23.03.02.exercise: Simulate delayed read projection after order placement; expose pending status and later convergence.
23.03.02.negative: UI falsely declaring missing order permanent or authorization from stale data fails.
23.03.02.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.03.03.context: An app commits an order but crashes before broker publish.
23.03.03.concept: Transactional outbox stores the event in the same database transaction, then a relay publishes with retry.
23.03.03.exercise: In disposable DB design order/outbox atomic write; force relay crash after publish and inspect retry path.
23.03.03.negative: Order without outbox or unhandled duplicate relay delivery fails.
23.03.03.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.03.04.context: A broker delivers the same event twice.
23.03.04.concept: Consumers need durable idempotency and conflict handling; in-memory dedupe only models the invariant.
23.03.04.exercise: Run idempotentConsumer with event e amount 5 twice, then e amount 6; plan DB uniqueness transaction.
23.03.04.positive: Total remains 5; exact duplicate is ignored.
23.03.04.negative: Same ID with different content conflicts; process restart is unqualified.
23.03.04.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.03.05.context: Checkout coordinates payment and shipment across services.
23.03.05.concept: A saga sequences local transactions and compensations; compensation is a business action, not distributed rollback.
23.03.05.exercise: Design reserve, charge, ship steps and payment failure compensation; record idempotency keys.
23.03.05.positive: Failed charge releases reservation via a retriable compensation.
23.03.05.negative: Compensation failure without recovery state or double charge fails.
23.03.05.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.03.06.context: A new event field reaches old consumers.
23.03.06.concept: Schema evolution requires explicit versioning and compatible defaults or separate message versions.
23.03.06.exercise: Create v1 and v2 synthetic messages with optional field; test old/new consumers and unknown version denial.
23.03.06.negative: Incompatible field removal or unknown version silently processed fails.
23.03.06.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.03.07.context: A broker redelivers messages after lost acknowledgement.
23.03.07.concept: At-least-once can duplicate, at-most-once can lose; exactly-once claims have a specific system boundary.
23.03.07.exercise: Simulate ack loss and duplicate delivery using idempotentConsumer; distinguish consumer state from external email side effect.
23.03.07.positive: Duplicate does not increment local total.
23.03.07.negative: Claiming exactly-once external delivery without evidence fails.
23.03.07.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.03.08.context: A learner builds a reliable order-event flow.
23.03.08.concept: Reliable integration combines transactional outbox, retry, durable inbox, explicit errors and idempotent effects.
23.03.08.exercise: Run local consumer tests; on disposable PostgreSQL rehearse outbox and P5 inbox with independent workers and recovery.
23.03.08.positive: Model handles duplicate; real DB integration must prove restart and atomicity.
23.03.08.negative: Duplicate effects or untracked uncertain commit block qualification.
23.03.08.boundary: In-memory synthetic idempotency model; no broker, durable store, transactional outbox or exactly-once side-effect evidence.

23.04.01.context: Two replicas cannot communicate during a write.
23.04.01.concept: CAP describes consistency and availability during partitions, not a fixed pick-two menu under normal operation.
23.04.01.exercise: Sketch a partition between replicas; choose reject versus accept conflicting writes for inventory and explain business impact.
23.04.01.positive: Choice preserves the explicitly selected invariant under partition.
23.04.01.negative: Claiming both linearizable writes and unconditional availability under partition fails.
23.04.01.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.

23.04.02.context: A service instance is replaced with a new address.
23.04.02.concept: Discovery maps logical service identity to healthy endpoints; stale entries and health delays require bounded retries.
23.04.02.exercise: In disposable local fixture change endpoint registration and observe discovery refresh with one unhealthy instance.
23.04.02.positive: Healthy endpoint selected after bounded refresh.
23.04.02.negative: Infinite retries to stale address or unauthenticated discovery fails.
23.04.02.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.

23.04.03.context: A chain of services retries at every hop.
23.04.03.concept: Deadlines and retry budgets limit amplification; idempotency and transient-failure classification protect effects.
23.04.03.exercise: Run retryDecision with remainingMs zero, maxAttempts reached and idempotent false; model one retry layer.
23.04.03.positive: Retries stop at deadline, budget or unsafe operation.
23.04.03.negative: Retrying permanent failures or ambiguous non-idempotent writes fails.
23.04.03.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.

23.04.04.context: A team chooses NATS or Kafka for event transport.
23.04.04.concept: Brokers differ in durability, retention, ordering scope and consumption models; compare configured guarantees, not brands.
23.04.04.exercise: Define workload retention, replay, ordering and failure recovery requirements; test on isolated real broker if available.
23.04.04.positive: Chosen configuration meets the stated guarantees with evidence.
23.04.04.negative: Assuming core pub/sub provides durable replay without configuration fails.
23.04.04.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.

23.04.05.context: A large dataset is split across partitions.
23.04.05.concept: Partition key affects balance, query locality and ordering; hot keys and cross-partition invariants need attention.
23.04.05.exercise: Assign synthetic tenant workloads to partitions; introduce a hot tenant and compare load distribution.
23.04.05.positive: Skew is visible and mitigation justified.
23.04.05.negative: Hashing without checking hot keys or cross-partition queries fails.
23.04.05.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.

23.04.06.context: Users in two regions access shared data.
23.04.06.concept: Replication and request routing trade latency against consistency and recovery; define write authority.
23.04.06.exercise: Draw region A/B paths and simulate network delay, stale read and failover.
23.04.06.positive: Plan states write authority, consistency and failover behavior.
23.04.06.negative: Unmeasured latency or conflicting leaders cannot qualify design.
23.04.06.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.

23.04.07.context: A modular monolith has one expensive workload.
23.04.07.concept: Extract a service only when independent scaling, failure isolation or ownership outweighs network/operational cost.
23.04.07.exercise: Write an ADR comparing module optimization, worker extraction and service extraction using observed bottlenecks.
23.04.07.positive: Decision names measurable trigger and migration risks.
23.04.07.negative: Splitting solely because microservices are fashionable fails.
23.04.07.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.

23.04.08.context: A learner reviews a distributed order design.
23.04.08.concept: Review invariants, deadlines, partition behavior, observability, ownership and recovery before committing to complexity.
23.04.08.exercise: Run retryDecision and earlier boundary/consumer models; write failure matrix for timeout, duplicate, partition and unavailable dependency.
23.04.08.positive: Every failure has expected behavior, evidence and owner.
23.04.08.negative: Missing recovery for uncertain side effects or invented guarantees blocks acceptance.
23.04.08.boundary: Retry decision teaching model only; no network partition, broker, service discovery, replication or multi-region benchmark.
